tabulator: Nim library for generating plain-text tables (with Unicode and ANSI code support) MIT © 2026 Eryk J

Types

Alignment = enum
  Left,                     ## Text is left-padded (default).
  Center,                   ## Text is centred within the column width.
  Right                      ## Text is right-padded.
Cell alignment within its column. 
SortKey = object
  column*: int               ## 0-based column index. Use the value returned by `defineColumn`.
  order*: SortOrder          ## Sort direction. Defaults to `Ascending`.
  compare*: proc (a, b: string): int ## Optional comparator. If nil, cells are compared lexicographically
                                     ## after stripping ANSI escapes. Comparison is case-sensitive:
                                     ## uppercase letters sort before lowercase (byte order). Provide a
                                     ## custom comparator for case-insensitive, numeric, date, or
                                     ## semantic sorting.

One key in a multi-column sort specification.

Keys are applied in order: the first is the primary sort, later keys are tie-breakers.

SortOrder = enum
  Ascending,                ## Smallest first (default for `cmp`).
  Descending                 ## Largest first.
Sort direction for a SortKey. 
Table = ref object
A rendered table. Create with newTable, populate with defineColumn and addRow, output with renderTable.

Procs

proc addRow(t: Table; cells: seq[string]) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Append a row of data. Cells may contain ANSI escape sequences.

If cells.len exceeds the current column count, new slots are created to hold the extra cells. Those slots are undefined until defineColumn is called for them.

proc columnCount(t: Table): int {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Number of columns in the table. 
proc defineColumn(t: Table; title: string = ""; width: int = 0;
                  align: Alignment = Left): int {....raises: [ValueError],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Define a column slot.

If a slot exists that was created implicitly (by a row longer than the
current column set) but has no definition, that slot is filled in.
Otherwise a new slot is appended.

- `title`: Column header (may contain ANSI codes).
  If ALL column titles are empty, no header row is printed.
- `width`: Fixed width in display cells, or 0 for auto-size.
  `1` produces "…" when content is longer; `2` produces "x…"; etc.
- `align`: Cell alignment within the column.

Returns the 0-based position of the slot that was defined. Since
columns are never reordered or deleted, this value is stable and can
be reused as `SortKey.column`.

.. versionchanged:: 2.0.0
   Renamed from `addColumn`. Now returns the slot's 0-based index
   and fills the lowest-position undefined slot rather than always
   appending.
proc newTable(): Table {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Create a new empty table. 
proc numericCompare(a, b: string): int {....raises: [ValueError], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}

Convenience comparator: parse both strings as floats and compare.

Both strings must be valid numeric literals (whitespace around the number is ignored). Anything else raises ValueError. Formatting such as a leading $ must be stripped by the caller before supplying this comparator.

proc renderTable(t: Table; separator = false; width: int = 0;
                 outFile: File = stdout) {....raises: [IOError],
    tags: [ReadEnvEffect, WriteIOEffect], forbids: [].}
Render the table.
  • separator: if true, draw box-drawing borders between columns.
  • width: table width target.
    • 0 (default) → natural width. Fixed columns keep their width; auto columns size to content. On a terminal, if the natural width exceeds the terminal width, auto columns are shrunk so the table fits. A table is never stretched to fill the terminal.
    • > 0 → table is exactly that width (auto columns absorb slack or shortfall). Fixed columns are never resized. If fixed columns alone exceed width, the table overflows; terminal output clips the overflow, file output keeps it.
  • outFile: destination (default stdout).

Terminal vs. file:

  • Terminal output is clipped at the terminal width, and never exceeds min(width, terminalWidth()) when width > 0.
  • File output is not clipped; the file contains the whole table at its laid-out width.

Example:

import tabulator

var t = newTable()
let colProduct = t.defineColumn("Product", width = 20)
let colPrice   = t.defineColumn("Price", align = Right)
let colStock   = t.defineColumn("In Stock", align = Center)

t.addRow(@["Apple", "$2.50", "yes"])
t.addRow(@["Banana", "$1.20", "no"])
t.addRow(@["Cherry", "$15.00", "low"])

t.renderTable(separator = true)

proc sortRows(t: Table; keys: openArray[SortKey]): Table {.
    ...raises: [ValueError, Exception], tags: [RootEffect], forbids: [].}

Return a new Table with rows sorted by keys.

Keys are applied in order (first is primary, later keys are tie-breakers). If SortKey.compare is nil, cells are compared lexicographically after stripping ANSI escapes. Provide a custom comparator for numeric, date, or semantic sorting.

Rows are always sorted by their raw cell content, not by the formatted/truncated display output.

t is not modified. Rows outside keys' column range use the empty string for comparison.

proc stripAnsi(s: string): string {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Remove all ANSI escape sequences from s. A bare/invalid ESC is preserved (it is not a sequence).

Internal helper. Exported for tests and for advanced users writing ANSI-aware text tools. Prefer using renderTable, which calls this internally.
